extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting fiction to Granta (literary short-story/fiction authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors preparing fiction submissions to Granta magazine, emphasizing first-publication-only, timely high-craft literary work, and explicit length limits. Useful for writers aiming to match Granta's editorial priorities and stylistic expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial mission — power and urgency of story
rubrics_metrics.description: Granta's belief in the power and urgency of the story: the story's supreme ability to describe, illuminate and make real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should reflect Granta's commitment to storytelling that illuminates and makes experience or phenomena feel real and urgent on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely work
rubrics_metrics.description: Pieces 'that deal with the world as it is now, not what it was or what it will be.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors prefer fiction that engages with present realities or urgent contemporary concerns rather than historical pastiche or distant speculative futures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue-shaped-by-submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Granta tends to shape its issues around the work it receives, rather than asking authors to write to themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect themed calls; submit work on its own merits — the editorial team curates issues based on strong unsolicited pieces rather than pre-defined themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-publication only
rubrics_metrics.description: Original material, never previously published online or in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only work that has not been published anywhere before; simultaneous or prior publication disqualifies a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-craft literary fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should demonstrate descriptive force, urgency, and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granta looks for high literary craft: energetic, precise description; a sense of urgency in purpose and voice; and a distinct narrative perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for the 3k–6k window as the typical target for Granta; do not exceed 10,000 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a world real on the page
rubrics_metrics.description: A world must be made real on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction should conjure a convincing, textured setting and internal logic so readers feel immersed — beyond mere plot summary or glib scene-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentences must be load-bearing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every sentence should carry weight: contribute to meaning, character, tension, or atmosphere rather than filler or decorative padding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urgency test
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'urgency' test — does this need to exist now, in the world?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the piece has a temporal or cultural urgency that justifies its publication now; pieces lacking urgency risk being deemed irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive perspective and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctive perspective and voice are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should present an identifiable, original narrative voice or viewpoint that differentiates the work from common or derivative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent interests — hybrid forms, internationalism, political consciousness, reportage-tinged fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Granta often publishes hybrid forms, internationalist work, politically conscious pieces, and fiction with reportage influences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not mandatory, work that blends forms, engages international or political concerns, or carries a reportage-inflected approach aligns well with Granta's editorial profile.
